one_month_reasoning: Fiscal Q1 FY27 closed on 2026-10-02 and Seagate has reported its September quarter in the third/fourth week of October in prior years, so the FQ1 print and FQ2 guide very likely land inside the window (before 2026-11-01). Guide was $4.1B +/- $0.1B and $7.30 +/- $0.20 non-GAAP EPS; with price per EB rising ~20% y/y, nearline allocated into CY2028 and WD guiding to 55-56% GM, a beat-and-raise is the likely outcome, which argues for mild upside. Against that: the 2026-10-02 drop (-11%, from $945.57 to ~$842) was driven by a Nikkei report that Toshiba will spend ~JPY60bn to double HDD capacity by FY2027 and targets ~30% share; management will be pressed on pricing durability and the stock has shown repeated sector-wide 10%+ drawdowns (June, July 2) on supply-glut fears. Net: median slightly above spot (~$845, +1%) with monthly sigma ~19% (a touch below 75%/3.5 = 21% as the earnings event is the main swing factor and fundamentals are strong), roughly symmetric.

fair_value.method: Blend of 17x a haircut FY28 (Jun-2028) EPS of $48 (=$816, 50%), FY28 FCF/share $38 at a 4.5% FCF yield (=$844, 30%), and a mid-cycle check of $30 normalized EPS x 20x (=$600, 20%); blended ~$780 twelve months out.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: FY28 EPS $48 (consensus $55.37 haircut ~13% for Toshiba/WD supply response) x 17x

inputs_detail.derivation: Consensus FY28 EPS $55.37 [12]; haircut ~13% because Toshiba's JPY60bn plan to double capacity by FY2027 [2] and supplier capacity adds [6,7] cap the price-per-EB growth (+10% y/y Q4, ~+20% implied for Q1 [5]) that consensus extrapolates; Q1 FY27 guide $7.30 [1] annualizes ~$29 before further pricing.

Stock traded ~35x trailing-forward EPS in Sept [12]; peak-cycle storage multiples compress as investors anticipate supply response (see repeated selloffs on capacity news [13,14]); 17x on two-years-out EPS is mid-range for a cyclical with LTAs into 2028.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: FY28 FCF ~$8.9B / ~235M diluted shares = ~$38/share at 4.5% yield

inputs_detail.derivation: FCF ~80% of net income on FY28 EPS ~$48 x 235M shares (231M non-GAAP diluted [1] plus some exchangeable-note dilution [12]); capex light since Seagate grows exabytes via areal density not new fabs [5,13].
Above large-cap tech averages to reflect hyperscaler concentration and cyclicality [12], tempered by visible demand from ~$1trn 2027 hyperscaler capex [10].
Approx. Q1 FY27 guide $7.30 x 4 [1] i.e. assumes pricing plateaus at current levels without further increases; WD's similar 55% GM guide [4] supports this as a sustainable plateau rather than peak.
Applied to a non-peak earnings level; below the ~35x forward the market paid in Sept [12].

bear.story: Toshiba (+ WD) capacity adds and HAMR density gains loosen supply into 2028; hyperscaler capex digests in 2H 2027; price per EB flattens, LTA renewals at lower prices; market prices peak earnings at ~10x FY28 EPS of ~$45.

base.story: Pricing up high-teens through FY27, FY27 EPS ~$35-37, FY28 ~$48-52; Toshiba add is component-constrained and only partly incremental; multiple ~17-18x FY28 EPS.

bull.story: Hyperscaler capex >$1trn in 2027 keeps nearline sold out into 2029, HAMR 40TB+ drives lift margins to high-50s, FY28 EPS ~$60 at ~22x.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$500 (~10x a still-elevated FY28 EPS, ~40% below spot) the market would be pricing a real turn in HDD pricing: LTA renegotiations, Toshiba/WD capacity flooding nearline, or a hyperscaler capex cut, rather than ordinary sector volatility (prior 10-12% sector drawdowns recovered).

reasoning: Today's -11% ($945.57 to ~$842; close $837.52) was an industry event: a Nikkei report that Toshiba will invest ~JPY60bn to double HDD output by FY2027 and targets ~30% share from ~10%, hitting WDC too (-7 to -10%). Citi noted Toshiba depends on outside heads/media, and suppliers (Resonac media 160M->210M disks/yr, TDK heads +50%) are expanding, so component constraints are easing for everyone, which is the real medium-term risk: supply response in an oligopoly whose pricing power came from scarcity. Chain evidence is still strong: Seagate Q4 rev $3.6B (+48%), GM 52.7%, price/EB +10% y/y rising toward ~20% in the Q1 guide ($4.1B, $7.30 EPS), nearline allocated into CY2028; WD Q4 +44%, guiding Q1 +42-49% and 55-56% GM; street hard-drive prices up >100%; hyperscaler 2027 capex forecast near $1trn+. Consensus FY27 EPS $35.78, FY28 $55.37, PT $1,125. I haircut FY28 and apply cyclical multiples, getting fair value ~$780, slightly below spot, with scenario mean ~$890. Given 75% realized vol and repeated 10%+ sector drawdowns, I use a lognormal-ish ladder with median ~$830 and sigma ~0.6 (below realized vol since part of it was the up-move), giving P(>=838) ~0.49.
